## Vocabulary

<a id="RenderingModes"></a>

### The renderings of a document

`RenderingModes` · `src/page.ts:43`

The page shows a document in one of three renderings; the first is shown first. Its style sheet and its script know them by these words: the script is typed by them, so a word changed here stops it from compiling.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rendered` | The document as the page lays it out, in HTML, with its figures drawn |
| `markdown` | Its Markdown, as trame build writes it |
| `text` | Its plain text, as a command prints it in the terminal |

- Owner: trame
- Used by: [Show the graph](browser.md#ShowGraph), [Choice of rendering](#RenderingToggle)

<a id="PageDocument"></a>

### Document of the page

`PageDocument` · `src/page.ts:782` · status: **held**

The page as a document of its own: the DOCTYPE, the root element in the language of the page, a head (the encoding, the viewport, the host's fit, the title, the fonts, the style), a body (the shell, the scripts). As a fragment, for a host that gives the skeleton of the document (an artifact): the title, the host's fit, the fonts, the style, the shell, the scripts. The viewport is as wide as the device, not zoomed, and covers the whole screen; so does the host.

Section: Document

| Mark | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | `html` | The root element |
| `head` | `head` | What the document says of itself |
| `body` | `body` | What it shows |
| `title` | `title` | The title of the document |
| `style` | `style` | A style sheet written in the document |
| `meta` | `meta` | What the document says of itself, as a name and a content |
| `name` | `name` | The name of a meta element |
| `content` | `content` | Its content |
| `charset` | `charset` | The encoding of the document |
| `encoding` | `utf-8` | UTF-8, as the WHATWG Encoding standard labels it |
| `viewport` | `viewport` | How a mobile browser lays the page out (CSS Viewport Module Level 1) |
| `deviceWidth` | `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover` | As wide as the device, not zoomed, drawn under the notch and the rounded corners |
| `hostFit` | `claude:viewport-fit-sides` | What the host that shows the page as an artifact (claude.ai) reads to draw it |
| `cover` | `cover` | To the edges of the screen |

| Input | Writes | Checked |

## Decisions

<a id="MachineHighlighting"></a>

### Files for tools in the page

`MachineHighlighting` · `src/page.ts:142`

A file of JSON is shown with its parts coloured: a key (a text before a colon), a text, a literal, a number. The pattern finds them in the file's escaped text: the first group a text, the second the colon after a key, the third a literal, the fourth a number.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| pattern | (&quot;(?:[^&]\|&(?!quot;))*?&quot;)(\s*:)?\|\b(true\|false\|null)\b\|(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?) |
| flags | g |

- Decided by: trame
- Used by: [Show the graph](browser.md#ShowGraph)

<a id="PackedGraph"></a>

### A page carries its graph compressed

`PackedGraph` · `src/page.ts:172`

An exported page holds the graph at every date, each document written three times (HTML, Markdown, text): in JSON, about 15 MB a date. Compressed with gzip and written in base64, it is about 2 MB; the browser decompresses it itself (DecompressionStream), before the page shows its first document.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| format | gzip |
| encoding | base64 |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: The graph in JSON, as it is, a page of 15 MB a date: slow to open, and too big for some hosts; Fewer dates in a page, reading the graph at another date is what an exported page is for; A compression library in the page, every browser decompresses gzip itself
- Used by: [The browser's gzip](browser.md#BrowserDecompression), [gzip, with Node's zlib](platform.md#NodeCompression)

<a id="ThePage"></a>

### The page

`ThePage` · `src/page.ts:79`

Trame's page shows the graph in a browser, standalone (trame export) or live (trame dev). A side bar holds the brand, the state of the compilation, the dates the graph can be read at, the navigation between documents and views (a select on small screens); the main area holds a banner for the last change, the head of the document (its path and the choice of rendering) and the document. The page's program and its style sheet find these regions by the classes and identifiers their elements declare; the program receives the compiled graph, and the mode of trame dev, through globals of the window. Its colours and fonts are the decisions of appearance, written as CSS variables, light and dark; a theme the person chooses is an attribute of the root element. The value holds what several elements share: the class of the labels of the side bar, the attribute and the names of the themes, the prefix of the class of a status, the names of the globals, the name under which the browser keeps the person's place, the name of the files for tools among the documents, the view a reference opens when no document holds the node's card, and the prompt written before a command. The renderings of a document are a vocabulary.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| label | label |
| themeAttribute | data-theme |
| themes | { light: light, dark: dark } |
| statusClass | st- |
| globals | { packedBundle: TRAME_BUNDLE_GZIP, dev: TRAME_DEV } |
| memory | trame-page |
| machine | machine |
| nodeView | impact |
| prompt | $  |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: A page per document, the page must work without a server (trame export): one file holds the graph at every date and all its documents; A front-end framework, one program, assembled from the graph like the command line, is enough to show the intermediate format

## Architecture decision

<a id="StyleThroughVariables"></a>

### A style sheet writes no value

`StyleThroughVariables` · `src/page.ts:889` · status: **held**

The values of the page's appearance are decisions of the graph: the page writes them as variables before its style sheets, which hold only variables, names and keywords.

Context: A style sheet is a body like any other: a value written in it hides its meaning, and the sheet of the page held 355. CSS cannot import a value, but it reads a variable declared before it.

Consequences: Each family of measures is a decision of appearance, and the theme writes them in :root with the colours and the fonts; the page refuses a style that uses a variable it does not write. A media query cannot read a variable: the width of a narrow screen is a decision, which the page writes in the media rule around the second sheet. The lines of a grid are named, not numbered. The scale was taken as it was, so the page looks as it did; folding it is a change of decisions.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Folding the values into a lighter scale first | the page would have changed at the same time as its sheet was brought into the graph |
| Writing the rules as syntax elements | the sheet is where the appearance is chosen; two hundred rules spread over elements would hide it |
| An exception for style sheets | a value without its meaning is the same problem in a sheet as in code |

- Decided by: trame
- Serves: [A single source of truth](product.md#SingleSource)
- Applied by: [Style sheet of the page](#PageStyle), [Style sheet of a narrow screen](#NarrowScreenStyle), [Theme](#Theme), [Rules of a narrow screen](#NarrowScreenRule), [Page](#Page)
